doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Young women today don't know the struggle
summary: They agree today's young women have not been through what they did, though good ones come along now and then.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Like you said, she’s – if they’re not musicians, they do not understand. There’s no way they could understand. And you know what? There’s no way the young girls today can understand the way we understand either.
I don’t think they want to. But anyway, I may be wrong.

No, because, see, they’re in a position where they don’t feel like they have to go – they know they don’t have to. They’re not going to go through what we went through to get – because there’s almost – we almost put it in their laps.
There are some girls that are very good. The bass player . . .
Oh yeah. What’s her name? She played with the Harper brothers and [?] when she was much younger.
Now and then a girl comes along.
